info.title: StreamLib runtime control API
info.description: Every operation a StreamLib runtime's control plane serves. `x-contract-version` is bumped only by a breaking change, and resets `x-contract-revision`, which an addition raises; an added method is also marked by its `x-since`. A runtime serves a client of its own version and a revision no higher than its own.

methods.name: discover
methods.summary: Answer the contract version and revision this runtime serves, its version and build id, and every method it serves.
methods.description: Answer `contract_version` and `contract_revision`, the contract this runtime serves, its `runtime_version` and `build_id`, and `operations`, every method it serves. A client sends the `contract_version` and `contract_revision` it was built against; another version, or a higher revision, is refused with error 3, whose data names the `older_side` to update, and the client is not served.

methods.name: subscribe_project_changes
methods.summary: Send this connection a `project_changed` notification for each change on the named projects' feeds.
methods.description: Subscribe the connection to the change feeds of `projects`, by UUID: from then on, each transaction applied to one, each action the runtime refuses on one, each media facts read it finishes, each making current of its `.venv` (`venv_made_current`) and each burst of files changed in its folder, an editor's saves among them, named under `files`, is sent as a `project_changed` notification, whoever made it, until the connection closes. A connection that falls behind, or a project whose folder changed in ways the OS did not name, is sent `missed`, and the client reads the change feed and lists the project's files and node types again. Served only on a connection that stays open; refused for an empty `projects`. Answers every project the connection is subscribed to.

methods.name: subscribe_stream_graph_changes
methods.summary: Send this connection a `stream_graph_changed` notification for each change in the named loaded streams' live graphs.
methods.description: Subscribe the connection to the live graphs of `streams`, by stream id, each loaded: from then on, each edit of one's graph is sent as a `stream_graph_changed` notification with `change` `edited`, each change of a node's state with `node_state_changed`, its `node` by graph `id` and its `node_state`, and each start, stop, pause or resume of its playback, or failure of one, with `playback_state_changed`, until the connection closes. A connection that falls behind, and a stream loaded again or unloaded, is sent `missed`, and the client reads the stream's `graph` again; the subscription follows the stream id across a reload. Served only on a connection that stays open; refused for an empty `streams` or a stream not loaded. Answers every stream the connection is subscribed to.

methods.name: subscribe_input_value_changes
methods.summary: Send this connection an `input_value_changed` notification for each change of the value an input of the named loaded streams reads.
methods.description: Subscribe the connection to the input values of `streams`, by stream id, each loaded: from then on, each change of the value an input reads while unlinked, set live or saved, is sent as an `input_value_changed` notification naming its `node` and `input`, with the `value` and `value_comes_from` `graph` renders for that input, until the connection closes; the caller of a set is sent it too. Changes are sent at most once each 33 ms for one input, the newest kept, and the last value is always sent. A connection that follows a stream's graph and has not subscribed here is sent `stream_graph_changed` `edited` for a value change instead, at most once each 500 ms for each stream; one that subscribed is sent no `edited` for a value set live, and `stream_graph_changed` `missed` when it may have missed changes, so it reads `graph` again. Served only on a connection that stays open; refused for an empty `streams` or a stream not loaded. Answers every stream the connection is subscribed to.

methods.name: subscribe_stream_action_changes
methods.summary: Send this connection a `stream_action_changed` notification each time a stream action changes.
methods.description: Subscribe the connection to every stream action: from then on, each time one is queued, moves on or ends, its id is sent as a `stream_action_changed` notification with `change` `changed`, and `describe_stream_action` describes it, until the connection closes. A connection that falls behind is sent `missed`, and the client describes each action it follows again. Served only on a connection that stays open. Answers `actions_under_way`, the id of each action queued or running as the subscription began.

methods.name: subscribe_project_log_records
methods.summary: Send this connection each new record of the named projects' logs as `project_log_records_written` notifications.
methods.description: Subscribe the connection to the logs of the projects in `project_directories`, each an absolute path: from then on, each time the runtime writes new records to one's log, which it does at most every 100 ms, `project_log_records_written` carries them, at most 500 to a notification, naming its `project_directory` as the connection spelled it. Each notification's `after` is the previous one's `next_after`, starting at the log's end as the project is subscribed; a client that read the log with `logs` to another cursor reads `logs` from its cursor `until` the notification's `next_after` instead, and appends the notifications after that. Served only on a connection that stays open; refused for an empty `project_directories`, or one that is relative or names no folder on this machine. Answers every project the connection is subscribed to, by its directory as the connection spelled it.

methods.name: describe_runtime
methods.summary: Describe this runtime: its version, its build id, how long it has been up and where it logs.
methods.description: Describe this runtime: its crate `version`, its `build_id` (`<version>+<git sha>.<per-build nonce>`, telling two builds of one version apart), `up_for_ms`, the monotonic milliseconds since its engine started — a restart resets it — and `runtime_log_directory`, the folder its own log is written to, `null` when it keeps none. Names no stream.

methods.name: list_streams
methods.summary: List every stream the runtime holds, by stream id, with its location and state.
methods.description: List every stream the runtime holds: its stream id as `stream`, its `display_name`, its `location` — its project directory, its project's UUID as `project` and its stream asset's UUID as `stream_asset`, `null` for a record an earlier runtime wrote — and its state: `running` (playing, or recorded playing and re-loaded playing at the runtime's next start), `stopped` (open with its playback stopped, its graph loaded to read and edit while its node count is set, until `start_playback`), `paused` (open with its playback paused by `pause_playback`, until `resume_playback`), `closed` (its project closed by `close_project`, not loaded, until `open_project`), `preparing` (an action that loads it — an `open_project`, `reload_project` or `start_playback` — is queued or under way on it, named by `action`, on its `step`: `reading_the_graph_documents`, `making_the_venv` or `starting`, `null` while it waits), `stopping` (a `stop_playback`, `close_project` or `remove_project` of its project is queued or under way on it, named by `action`, on the step `stopping`, `null` while it waits), or `failed` (its code, its venv, its load or its start failed, and held stopped from its document when that reads, its graph there to read and edit, until a play or a `reload_project` retries it; implicated in the runtime's last two crashes in a row, and held at a start from its document with none of its node code read until a `reload_project` of its project tries it; or recorded by an earlier runtime, never loaded, with `failed_because` saying to run it again and `remove_project` forgetting it), with the node count of its loaded graph (`null` when it is not loaded), `failed_because`, why a failed stream failed (`null` otherwise), and `capture_devices_whose_access_was_never_asked_for`, each of `camera` and `microphone` that a node of the loaded stream refused because nobody has asked the user for its access, as when the runtime re-loaded the stream on its own at its start (empty otherwise): a `close_project` then `open_project` of its project asks. Its `condition` answers its load, playback and health apart, whatever `state` says: `load` (`not_loaded`, `loading`, `loaded` — its graph held to read and edit, failed or not — or `unloading`), `playback` (`stopped`, `starting`, `playing`, `paused` or `stopping`), `health` (`healthy`, `degraded` while a node of it fails, raises or is not ready, or its graph document holds an edit its running graph did not take — kind `edit_not_live`, taken when its playback stops — whatever its playback, or `failed` until a recovery is made), and `diagnostics`, each problem behind its health: its `kind`, its `place` (`{"on": "stream"}`, a node by `node_id` and `node_name`, or a link by `from_node`, `from_port`, `to_node` and `to_port`), the runtime's `words` and the `recovery` that applies: `retry_the_load` (a `reload_project` of its project, or a `start_playback` while its graph is loaded), `fix_the_code`, `fix_the_dependencies`, `fix_the_link`, `restart_the_playback`, `remove_the_stream` (a `remove_project` of the project directory its record names) or `wait_for_the_node`. A kind or value this client does not know reads as the set's fallback: `other` for a kind, `not_loaded`, `stopped`, `failed` and `retry_the_load` for the rest.

methods.name: graph
methods.summary: Export a loaded stream's graph, or every loaded stream's, with each node's and link's state and each part not live yet marked.
methods.description: Export a loaded stream's current graph as JSON: the stream it was loaded as, its nodes by name with their types, the values their graph document holds for their inputs (`input_values`) and their ports, each input with the `value` it reads while unlinked and `value_comes_from`, where that value comes from: `live`, `saved` or `default`, or `wire` with no `value` when a link feeds it; a port whose pin type is exact names it as `pin_type`, with its `flow`. Its links by node and port, each link between two typed pins with `free_conversion` `true` where the input reads the output as its own type at no cost and the `warnings` that judgement gave, with each node's and link's live state and counters beside them, and this machine's name (`machine`), the first part of `<machine>/<stream id>/<node>/<port>`. A fragment — a graph generator's stored output — renders as one node of `kind` `fragment` whose ports are its Graph Input and Output nodes' and whose `fragment` holds its own nodes and links, a fragment inside it rendered the same way; its nodes run under their path of names, `look/soft/blur`. A node that keeps a state carries its `health` in its `components` (`healthy`, `not_ready`, `raising` or `failed`) with the `diagnostics` behind it, left out while it has none; a fragment's own node carries neither. Each stream graph carries its `condition`, as `list_streams` answers it. While a stream's graph document holds an edit its running graph did not take, its graph is the document's: each node and link the running graph holds rendered live, and each other drawn as the document writes it with `live: false` until the stream's playback stops and takes it; `live` is absent on every node and link that runs. Without `stream`, `{machine, streams}` holds every loaded stream's graph.

methods.name: transact
methods.summary: Apply operations on one project's stream graphs as one transaction, whole or not at all.
methods.description: Apply operations on the graphs of one project's loaded streams as one transaction by its `author`: applied in order, whole or not at all, to each running stream, and with `mode` `commit`, the default, written to each stream's graph document and recorded as one commit on the project's history, which `undo` reverses as one. Answers `mode`, the `transaction` and `commit` recording a committed edit, each operation as applied, `added_nodes` with each new node's UUID and the name it took, and `connected_links` with each new link's `state` — `pending`, `wired`, or `error` with its `error_reason`. Refused whole, in the runtime's own words, with nothing changed. A `live` transaction sets each input of a node once, since each value set live is published as its own write: one setting the same input of the same node twice is refused with `refused` at its second set, before anything is applied. A config value `{"asset": "<uuid>"}` must name an asset the project holds. An `add_node` may give its node an `as`, which later operations of the same transaction name the node by. The transaction is announced on the project's change feed, the resource `list_assets` names as `transactions_resource_uri`.

methods.name: add_node
methods.summary: Add a node to a loaded stream's graph by its type's import path, as one transaction.
methods.description: Add a node to a loaded stream's graph by its type's import path, as one transaction, the runtime making the node's UUID. A Python type is named `module:QualifiedClassName` and must be importable by the stream's own interpreter — a module in the stream's project, or a package installed in its venv: the runtime never imports it, and describes it in that interpreter the first time it is added; each add spawns it in its own node interpreter, which imports the module fresh. The type's port declaration is read when it is first described and kept; to change a type's ports, add it under a new class name.

methods.name: connect
methods.summary: Link an output port to an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction.
methods.description: Link an output port to an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction, each end a node's UUID and a port name `graph` lists under that node's `ports`. A stream reads another stream's track at a relay through a `MoqTrackReceive` node. A link is spliced in by connecting a new node on both sides, then disconnecting the link it replaces — or all three in one `transact`. A link that would close a loop of function nodes with no `tatolab.stream:PreviousValue` node in it adds one and runs through it: the result names it under `added_nodes` and both of its links under `connected_links`. Two ends that both state a pin type connect when the input takes what the output sends: the same type; a Texture whose every pixel format is one the input lists, an input listing none taking any, and an output listing none connecting to an input that lists some; an encoded video or audio stream or an Asset whose every codec or media is one the input lists, an input listing none taking any, and an output listing none connecting only to an input that lists none; a Menu into a Menu, whatever options each lists; or a type the input reads from the output's for free: Boolean, Integer and Float among themselves, a Vector into a Vector or a Color, one number into a Vector or a Color, a Menu into a String. Any other pair is refused with `link_pin_types_do_not_connect`, naming both types and either the node or nodes to place between the two ends or that no node type converts between them. A link a saved graph document already holds that these rules refuse is kept when the stream loads, as long as its two ports' families match, and the runtime logs the refusal. A link into an input that is a setting is refused with `input_takes_no_wire`; set its value with `set_node_input_value`. These pin type rules judge a link in the stream's own graph; a link inside a placed stream, under a non-empty `level`, is not judged by them yet.

methods.name: check_link
methods.summary: Answer what `connect` would answer for one link in a loaded stream, changing nothing.
methods.description: Answer what `connect` would answer for one link in a loaded stream, judged against its running graph by the same rules, changing neither the graph nor the project's history: it takes `connect`'s `stream`, `level`, `source` and `target`. `outcome` is one of the values its schema lists, each described there; with `refused` comes the whole `refusal` `connect` would answer, its `refusal_code` among them, such as `link_pin_types_do_not_connect` or `input_takes_no_wire`. A link that needs a convert node is refused today, as `connect` refuses it. `warnings` lists what the link would do that a person may not expect, none of which blocks it. Three links are not checked yet, and `check_link` itself fails on them: one under a non-empty `level`, one reaching a fragment node, and one closing a loop of function nodes, which `connect` closes through a `PreviousValue` node it adds.

methods.name: check_link_candidates
methods.summary: Answer what `check_link` would answer for each link between one placed port and many candidate ports, changing nothing.
methods.description: Answer, in one call, what `check_link` would answer for each link between one placed port of a loaded stream and many candidate ports of the other direction, changing nothing. `from` is the placed port: `{"output": {"node": …, "port": …}}`, each candidate then an input, or `{"input": …}`, each candidate then an output. `among` is `"placed_ports"`, every such port of every node at the level; `"node_type_ports"`, every such port of every node type the stream has described: the built-ins, the installed modules' types, and the project's own types once a node of each has been placed, to learn which node type can take an output before placing one; or `{"ends": [...]}`, these ends alone, each `{"kind": "placed_port", "node", "port"}` or `{"kind": "node_type_port", "node_type", "port"}`. Each entry of `candidates` holds its `end` and its `check`, which is exactly what `check_link` answers for that link. A node type's port is judged as the port of a node an `add_node` with no input values would place: one of several types by the one that connects best, any type, or a type found from a link or a setting, as the placed port's type, the last with the warning `type_found_only_once_placed`. A candidate `connect` would refuse is left out unless `include_refused` is true. A candidate `check_link` would not check yet is listed under `not_checked` with why: one reaching a fragment node, or a port of a fragment or a graph interface node type; one closing a loop of function nodes; and a port of a node type the stream has not described yet, which this call never describes, so place a node of it first. A non-empty `level` is refused, as `check_link` refuses it, and so is a `from` naming a node the graph does not hold or a port its node does not have in that direction.

methods.name: import_graph_generator
methods.summary: Run one of the project's `@graph_generator` functions in the stream's own interpreter and place what it builds in a loaded stream's graph as a fragment node, as one transaction.
methods.description: Run one of the project's `@graph_generator` functions in the stream's own interpreter and place what it builds in a loaded stream's graph as a fragment node, as one transaction: its generator as `type`, its promoted settings as `config`, and the nodes and links it built stored under `fragment`, each node with a UUID of its own. Run again under the name of a fragment the graph holds, it refreshes that fragment with the fresh run: each node it builds keeps the UUID of the node of the same name it built before, so links into the fragment and the graph's history hold. A generator that raises, refuses, or is not found is refused with its traceback, nothing changed. Answers as `transact` does, a new fragment node under `added_nodes`; undo restores the fragment as it was.

methods.name: remove_node
methods.summary: Remove a node from a loaded stream's graph by its UUID, as one transaction, stopping it.
methods.description: Remove a node from a loaded stream's graph by its UUID, as one transaction, stopping it; its links go with it, and undo brings both back.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.summary: Take out the link between an output port and an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction, each end a node's UUID and a port name.
methods.description: Take out the link between an output port and an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction, each end a node's UUID and a port name.

methods.name: set_node_config
methods.summary: Replace a node's config whole, as one transaction, applied to the running node at the stream's next commit. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`.
methods.description: Replace a node's config whole, as one transaction, applied to the running node at the stream's next commit. A config value `{"asset": "<uuid>"}` references an asset of the project, which then cannot be deleted while the reference stands. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`, which sets one input or setting: this call is one such set for each key it names, and on a node type that still takes a config, one that takes off each config key it does not name.

methods.name: set_pin_value
methods.summary: Set the value one of a node's inputs holds while no link feeds it, as one transaction. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`.
methods.description: Set the value one of a node's inputs holds while no link feeds it, as one transaction; the value is saved in the graph document as a link is. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`, which this call is one set of.

methods.name: set_node_input_value
methods.summary: Set the value one input of one node holds while no link feeds it, saved or live, as one transaction.
methods.description: Set the value one input of one node holds while no link feeds it, as one transaction, on every kind of node: an input `graph` lists under the node's `ports.inputs`, or a setting it holds among its `input_values`. With `mode` `commit`, the default, the value is saved in the graph document, set on the running node and recorded as one commit that undo reverses to the value it replaced; with `mode` `live` it is set on the running node alone. A live value follows the lifetime its input declares: on a `kept` input, the default, it outlives Stop, the project's close and a restart of the runtime, and is held while the stream is stopped for its next Play; on a `reset` input it is taken off at Stop, so the input reads its saved value again, and a live set on it while the stream is stopped is refused with `node_not_running` and `not_running_because` `playback_stopped`. Omit `value`, or send `null`, to take the value off, so the input reads its declared default. The value is checked before anything is set: an input the node does not have is refused with `port_not_found`, an input that takes only a link with `input_takes_no_value`, and a value of another type or outside its range with `input_value_not_valid`, never clamped; each refusal names the node and the input. A set on an input a link feeds is kept and answered under `overridden_by_links`, since the link's messages are what the node reads. A config field takes a link once `set_exposed_config_fields` exposes it as an input. Omit `node` to set one of the stream's own inputs at the stream's own level: `input` names the port a top-level `GraphInput` declares, the set is made on that node's `value` input, which takes a value of the family the `GraphInput` declares, a number within its `range`, and lasts as its `lifetime` says; a name no `GraphInput` declares is refused with `port_not_found`, naming the stream's inputs. It is also an operation of `transact`, where a `live` transaction sets each input of a node once: a second live set of the same input is refused with `refused`, since each value set live is published as its own write.

methods.name: rename_node
methods.summary: Give a node another name, a label, as one transaction.
methods.description: Give a node another name, a label, as one transaction; the node keeps its UUID, which every address names it by. Refused while another node's config names it by its name.

methods.name: set_studio_fields
methods.summary: Replace what Tato Studio draws a node with — canvas position, group, comment, colour, collapsed, and a client's own `metadata` — as one transaction, the old fields replaced whole.
methods.description: Replace what Tato Studio draws a node with — canvas position, group, comment, colour, collapsed, and a client's own `metadata` — as one transaction, the old fields replaced whole. The fields are held to the studio contract: a key of the wrong shape, or any key outside it, is refused by name. It changes nothing that runs.

methods.name: set_exposed_config_fields
methods.summary: Replace the config fields a node takes as inputs, as one transaction.
methods.description: Replace the config fields a node takes as inputs, as one transaction. Each is a number or bool field of the node's config schema and becomes an input of the field's name: linked, it drives the field, a function node reading it at each evaluation and a process node taking each new value as a live config update; unlinked, it reads the node's config. A field still linked cannot be taken off. On a node type that takes no config it records nothing, and refuses a name that is not one of the node's inputs. It makes a config field linkable; `set_node_input_value` sets a field's value.

methods.name: add_group
methods.summary: Make a labelled group of nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction.
methods.description: Make a labelled group of nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction: a title, a description and a colour Tato Studio frames the nodes with, so the next reader knows what they do. It changes nothing that runs. Each node joins it by holding the group's UUID as its `studio.group`; a node of another group is refused, and a node leaves or joins later through `set_studio_fields`. Answers as `transact` does, the new group's UUID under `added_groups`.

methods.name: set_group_fields
methods.summary: Set a labelled group's title, description or colour, as one transaction.
methods.description: Set a labelled group's title, description or colour, as one transaction; a field omitted is kept. Its nodes stay as they are.

methods.name: collapse_selection_into_subgraph
methods.summary: Collapse nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, into one subgraph node, as one transaction.
methods.description: Collapse nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, into one subgraph node, as one transaction with `mode` `commit`: the nodes and the links between them are saved as a new stream of the project, `streams/<name>.graph.json`, and placed by reference where they were, so editing inside the subgraph edits that stream everywhere it is placed, and it runs only where it is placed. Each link that crossed the selection is carried through a `GraphInput` or `GraphOutput` of the new stream, named `<node>-<port>` and of the family the running stream declares at the link's source, so the stream runs the same nodes, each under the subgraph's name (`sub/blur`) and the UUID its placement gives it. Answers as `transact` does, the subgraph node under `added_nodes`; undo gives back the exact earlier graph document and takes the new stream out again, refused while another stream places it.

methods.name: unlock_subgraph
methods.summary: Unlock a subgraph node of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction.
methods.description: Unlock a subgraph node of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction: its nodes and the links between them become plain nodes of its level, its `GraphInput` and `GraphOutput` nodes go, and each link into or out of one of its ports is carried straight to the node it fed or read. A graph generator's output unlocked this way is no longer refreshed. A placed stream's nodes come back as a copy under new UUIDs that no edit of that stream then reaches, and the stream stays in the project, running as its own stream once nothing places it. Refused for a node of the subgraph named as a node of the level is; undo gives back the exact earlier graph document.

methods.name: add_note
methods.summary: Place a canvas note on a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction.
methods.description: Place a canvas note on a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction: text at a position and size Tato Studio draws it at, beside the nodes rather than on one. It changes nothing that runs. Answers as `transact` does, the new note's UUID under `added_notes`.

methods.name: set_note_fields
methods.summary: Set a canvas note's text, position or size, as one transaction.
methods.description: Set a canvas note's text, position or size, as one transaction; a field omitted is kept.

methods.name: remove_note
methods.summary: Take a canvas note off a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction.
methods.description: Take a canvas note off a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction. Undo puts it back as it was.

methods.name: remove_group
methods.summary: Take out a labelled group, as one transaction.
methods.description: Take out a labelled group, as one transaction: its nodes stay, ungrouped. Undo brings the group back with every node that belonged to it.

methods.name: open_project
methods.summary: Queue the open of a project: its streams are loaded and held with their playback stopped.
methods.description: Open the project in `project_directory`: queue its open on its own stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. The open reads its `tatolab-project.json` and each stream asset's graph document, makes the project's `.venv` with the uv the runtime carries when its `.venv/bin/python` does not run — however long uv takes — then loads each stream under its stream id, `<project>-<stream>-<hash>`, the hash over the project's UUID and the stream asset's UUID, and holds it with its playback stopped, recording each stream stopped or failed: a graph document that does not load, or a load that is refused, with its reason, and a `.venv` uv cannot make — uv's own words — failing every stream of the project. It starts no node. Once it is done, `graph`, every graph edit and the node catalog answer for each stream, and `start_playback` plays the project. The project stays open, held stopped or playing, across the runtime's restarts until `close_project`. It opens a project that was never opened, one `close_project` closed, and one whose every stream failed, retrying them. One project's actions run one at a time, in the order they were queued; different projects' run side by side. Follow the action with `describe_stream_action`, its streams with `list_streams` — `preparing`, with the action and its `step`, until it ends — and its records with `logs` given `action`. A directory that does not exist or holds no `tatolab-project.json` fails the action, never the call. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project open once its queued actions run, which `reload_project` refreshes.

methods.name: reload_project
methods.summary: Queue a soft reload of an open project from disk, keeping its playback.
methods.description: Softly reload the open project in `project_directory` from disk: queue the load on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. It re-reads every stream asset's graph document. While the project's node code — its `.py` files, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and views' `tatolab_view.json` — is as it was at a stream's load, the stream stays loaded and its graph is brought to its document in place, each node matched by its UUID, so only the nodes and links that changed change; otherwise the stream is loaded again under its same id, keeping its display name. A stream whose graph document is gone is unloaded and forgotten, a failed stream is loaded again, and the project's `.venv` is synced only when its dependency files changed or its `.venv/bin/python` does not run. The project keeps its playback: a playing project's streams start playing, a paused one's start paused, and a stopped one's are held stopped. `tatolab dev` asks for it on each save. A hard reload is `close_project` then `open_project`. Follow it as `open_project`'s open. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project that is not open, which `open_project` opens.

methods.name: close_project
methods.summary: Queue the close of an open project: its streams are unloaded and stay closed until it is opened.
methods.description: Close the open project in `project_directory`: queue the close on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, it ends the playback of every stream of the project, unloads each, forgets its function-node state, and records each closed, so the runtime leaves the project unloaded across its restarts until `open_project` opens it again. It deletes nothing: the project's files, its `.venv` and what uv synced into it stay. Its streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends, then `closed`; follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Each recorded stream carries the close on its record until it has run, so a runtime crash finishes it at the next start. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project that is not open once its queued actions run.

methods.name: remove_project
methods.summary: Queue the removal of a project from the runtime: its streams are stopped and their records forgotten.
methods.description: Queue the removal of the whole project in `project_directory` on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`: once the project's earlier actions have run, it unloads every loaded stream of the project and forgets every record of it, so the runtime no longer re-loads any of them, and deletes no file. `delete_asset` on a stream asset unloads and forgets that one stream. The project's streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends; follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project the runtime holds no stream of.

methods.name: start_playback
methods.summary: Queue the start of an open project's playback.
methods.description: Start the playback of the open project in `project_directory`: queue it on the project's stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, each stream the project holds stopped starts fresh from the graph it holds, edits made while stopped included, reading no graph document and making no `.venv`: every node instance is made anew, so only the state a node persists itself carries over from an earlier playback. Each stream is recorded running, so the runtime plays the project again across its restarts until `stop_playback`. A project plays or stops as a whole: no tool plays or stops one of its streams. Follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute; a project that is not open, which `open_project` opens; a paused project, which `resume_playback` resumes; and a project that plays once its queued actions run, which `stop_playback` stops.

methods.name: stop_playback
methods.summary: Queue the stop of a project's playback, its streams staying loaded.
methods.description: Stop the playback of the whole project in `project_directory`: queue the stop on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action` beside the `project_directory`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, it ends the playback of every loaded stream of the project — every node instance, device claim, function-node state and the clock torn down — keeps each stream's graph loaded, so `graph`, every graph edit and the node catalog still answer for it, and records each stopped, so the runtime holds the project open and stopped across its restarts until `start_playback` plays it again from the graph it holds. Its streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends; follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Each recorded stream carries the stop on its record until it has run, so a runtime crash finishes it at the next start. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, a project whose removal is queued, and a project none of whose streams plays once the actions queued before it run.

methods.name: pause_playback
methods.summary: Pause a playing project's playback at once.
methods.description: Pause the playback of the whole project in `project_directory` at once, never waiting behind an action on its queue, and answer the `project_directory` and, as `streams`, the id of each loaded stream this call paused. Every node of each loaded stream holds its state and processes nothing, and a scaled or stepped stream clock holds where it stands, opening no step, while a real-time clock is the machine's own and runs on; the streams stay loaded and are `paused` in `list_streams`, and a graph edit made meanwhile is applied and compiles on `resume_playback`. The project stays paused until `resume_playback`, `stop_playback`, `close_project` or `remove_project`: a stream a `reload_project` loads meanwhile, the one `tatolab dev` asks for on a save among them, starts paused. Pause is recorded, so a runtime restart re-loads the project paused. Pausing a paused project pauses nothing more. Refused: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project none of whose streams plays — none loaded, or each held stopped, which `start_playback` plays — and whose last action queued is not a `start_playback`.

methods.name: resume_playback
methods.summary: Resume a paused project's playback at once.
methods.description: Resume the paused playback of the project in `project_directory` at once and answer the `project_directory` and, as `streams`, the id of each stream this call resumed: every node carries on from the state it held, each held stream clock carries on from the stream time it was held at, and each stream compiles the graph edits made while it was paused, a compile that fails logged in the project's `logs` as a live edit's is. Refused: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project that is not paused.

methods.name: describe_stream_action
methods.summary: Describe one stream action by its id: its state, its step and each stream it reached.
methods.description: Describe the stream action `action`: its project, `kind` (`open`, `load`, `start_playback`, `stop`, `close`, `remove`, `delete`, `reload_at_start` or `make_venv_current`), `state` — `queued` behind the project's earlier actions, `in_progress` on its `step` (`reading_the_graph_documents`, `making_the_venv`, `starting`), `done`, `failed` with `failed_because`, or `cancelled` by `cancel_stream_action` — its `venv_sync`, what its latest uv sync of the project's `.venv` has done, read from uv's own lines from the moment uv starts and kept once it ends, `null` for an action that has not synced: its `phase` (`resolving`, `downloading`, `building`, `installing`, `installed`), `packages_resolved`, `packages_prepared` and `packages_installed` as uv counts them, `downloads_started` and `downloads_done` of the downloads uv names — only those over about a MiB — and under `packages` each package uv named, first named first, by `name`, `version` once uv names it, `kind` (`distribution` or `python_interpreter`), `state` (`downloading`, `downloaded`, `building`, `built`, `installed`, `uninstalled`) and `download_size_bytes` as uv states it; uv names no byte of a download as it arrives — and `streams`, each stream its project's graph documents named by `stream` id and `display_name`, with its `state` `running`, `stopped` or `failed` once the action took it in. Followed live as the resource `streamlib://stream-action/<action>`, which a `subscriptions/listen` naming it is sent `notifications/resources/updated` for each time the action changes. The runtime holds every queued and running action and the last 64 finished ones of each project; an older one is refused, its records still in the project's `logs`.

methods.name: cancel_stream_action
methods.summary: Cancel one stream action that is still queued or under way.
methods.description: Cancel the stream action `action`, the only way an action ends early; nothing replaces or edits a queued one. A queued action is dropped from its project's queue, its pending mark taken off each stream's record so the record stays as it was, and answers `cancelled`. A running `open`, `load`, `reload_at_start` or `make_venv_current` answers `in_progress` and stops at the step it is on — a running uv sync is killed and a half-made `.venv` removed — then ends `cancelled`: a stream it was loading is recorded failed, and the streams it had not reached stay as recorded. Refused for a running `stop`, `close` or `remove`, whose unload has begun and cannot be cut short, which ends `done`; for an action already finished; and for one the runtime does not hold.

methods.name: rename_project
methods.summary: Rename a project, as one transaction on its history.
methods.description: Rename a project, as one transaction by `author` on its history that undoes like any edit: its `name` in `tatolab-project.json` changes, and its UUID, its folder and its streams' ids stay as they are. Answers how people see the project now, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a blank name.

methods.name: set_project_description
methods.summary: Describe a project, or clear its description, as one transaction on its history.
methods.description: Describe a project, or clear its description, as one transaction by `author` on its history that undoes like any edit: its `description` in `tatolab-project.json`, served by `list_assets` as `project_description`. Answers how people see the project now, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: set_project_cover
methods.summary: Give a project a cover, or take it away, as one transaction on its history.
methods.description: Give a project a cover, or take it away, as one transaction by `author` on its history that undoes like any edit: its `cover` in `tatolab-project.json` names a media asset the project holds by its UUID, served by `list_assets` as `project_cover`. An image a person picks, or a frame a viewer showed, is first imported with `import_asset` and then named here; the asset cannot be deleted while it is the cover. Answers how people see the project now, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for an asset the project does not hold, or one that is not a media asset.

methods.name: duplicate_project
methods.summary: Duplicate a project into a folder that does not exist yet, as a project of its own.
methods.description: Duplicate a project into `into`, a folder that does not exist yet, as a project of its own: every file a copy of it carries, its `imports/` included, and its whole history, so its edits can still be undone in the copy, under a new project UUID and the name `<name> copy`, the duplicate recorded as a commit on its history by `author`. Its `.venv` and the rest of its `.tatolab/` stay behind, and the duplicate is not opened: `open_project` opens it. Answers the duplicate's `project_directory`, `project`, `project_name` and `commit`. Refused, nothing left at `into`, for a relative `into`, one that exists, and one inside the project.

methods.name: delete_project
methods.summary: Queue the deletion of a whole project.
methods.description: Delete the whole project in `project_directory`: queue its deletion on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action` beside the `project_directory`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, it unloads every loaded stream of the project and forgets every record of it, as `remove_project` does, then moves the project's folder to this machine's Trash, from which its owner can put it back. Its streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends; follow it with `describe_stream_action`, which answers `failed` with why when the folder could not be moved. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a folder holding no `tatolab-project.json`.

methods.name: list_assets
methods.summary: List a project's assets, ordered by path.
methods.description: List a project's assets, ordered by path: each by its `asset` UUID, its `kind` (`stream`, `media`, `scene` or `data`), its `path` in the project, the SHA-256 and size of its bytes, its `import_settings`, and what the runtime has read from its bytes — `media_facts_state` (`read`, `reading`, `unreadable` with `media_facts_unreadable_because`, or `null` for a stream), `media_facts` and `preview`, as `describe_asset` answers them, each from what is already read, an asset not yet read queued for a read — with the project's UUID, `project_name`, `project_description`, `project_cover` — the UUID of the image asset it is shown by — and `project_last_edited_at`, when its history last changed in seconds since the Unix epoch, each `null` when it has none, and `transactions_resource_uri`, its change feed. `kind` narrows to one kind. Refused for a folder with no `tatolab-project.json`.

methods.name: read_project_changes
methods.summary: Read a project's change feed as it stands: its newest transactions, refused actions and media facts reads.
methods.description: Read the change feed of the project in `project_directory`, opening it as `list_assets` does, as the resource `list_assets` names as `transactions_resource_uri` renders it: the project's UUID as `project`, its `project_directory`, and under `transactions` its newest 64 transactions, the actions refused and the assets whose media facts were read since the runtime started, newest first, each tagged by `status`. `subscribe_project_changes` sends a `project_changed` notification for each change after it, and `missed` when changes went unsent, after which the feed is read again and the project's files listed again. Refused for a folder with no `tatolab-project.json`.

methods.name: describe_asset
methods.summary: Describe one asset of a project.
methods.description: Describe one asset of a project: its UUID, kind, path, the SHA-256 and size of its bytes, its import settings, `file_at_its_path`, whether a file is at its path, and what the runtime has read from its bytes, which it reads once per SHA-256 after an import or a replace and keeps in the project's `.tatolab/`. `media_facts_state` is `read`, `reading` — a read queued or under way, after which the project's change feed carries a `media_facts_read` entry — `unreadable`, with why in `media_facts_unreadable_because`, or `null` for a stream asset. `media_facts` carries `duration_ms`; `video` with `pixel_width`, `pixel_height`, `frames_per_second` and `codec`; `audio` with `sample_rate_hz`, `channel_count` and `codec`; `image` with `pixel_width` and `pixel_height`; `lut` with `lut_1d_size` or `lut_3d_size`, `domain_min` and `domain_max`; and `scene` — each `null` when the file does not hold or state it. `preview` is the size and `media_type` of the picture `read_asset_preview` answers, `null` when the asset has none.

methods.name: read_asset_preview
methods.summary: Read an asset's preview picture.
methods.description: Read an asset's preview picture, which the runtime makes from its bytes and keeps in the project's `.tatolab/`: a PNG at most 512 pixels on its longest edge, answered as `content_base64`, standard base64 with padding, with its `media_type`, `pixel_width`, `pixel_height` and `byte_len`. An image has one; video, audio, a LUT, a scene and other data have none yet, as `describe_asset`'s `preview` being `null` says. Refused while the runtime is still reading the asset's bytes — `describe_asset`'s `media_facts_state` reads `reading`, and the project's change feed carries a `media_facts_read` entry once it is done — for an asset with no preview, and for a stream asset.

methods.name: import_asset
methods.summary: Import a file as a new asset of a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Import a file as a new asset of the project at `asset_path`, or, with no `asset_path`, in its kind's folder of the project's standard layout — `media/` for video, audio and images, `scenes/` for USD, glTF and other 3D scenes, `data/` for everything else — under `file_name` or the source file's own name, numbered `<name>-2.<extension>`, `-3`, … past a name an asset or another file already takes there. Answers the `asset`, with the UUID the runtime made for it, which every later relocation keeps, and the `path` it landed at, and the `transaction` and `commit` that record it. The bytes are copied once, to `asset_path`, and only the asset's sidecar, `<asset_path>.asset.json`, enters history. `source` is a file on this machine by absolute path, copied there, or an upload in the project's `.tatolab/uploads/` by its SHA-256, moved there; a file already at `asset_path` is imported in place. Undoing the import removes the file at `asset_path`, one imported in place included, and nothing keeps its bytes. Refused whole, with nothing written, for a path another asset or another file holds, a path outside the project, and a stream, which is never imported.

methods.name: relocate_asset
methods.summary: Move or rename an asset inside its project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Put an asset at another path of the project, renaming it, moving it to another folder or both, its sidecar going with it, as one transaction; the asset keeps its UUID. Answers the asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: delete_asset
methods.summary: Delete an asset from a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Stop tracking an asset as one transaction: its file and sidecar leave the project, and nothing keeps its bytes, so undoing the transaction brings back its sidecar and the asset reads missing until its file is at its path again. A stream asset's graph document leaves the project, recorded in the transaction so an undo writes it back, and its stream is unloaded and forgotten. Refused while a stream's graph document references the asset, the refusal naming each document. Answers the asset as it was, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: set_asset_settings
methods.summary: Replace an asset's import settings, as one transaction.
methods.description: Replace an asset's import settings whole, as one transaction. Answers the asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: replace_asset
methods.summary: Replace an asset's bytes, as one transaction.
methods.description: Put new bytes at an asset's path as one transaction: the asset keeps its UUID, path, kind and settings, so every node referencing it reads the new bytes at its next load, and its sidecar records their SHA-256 and size. `source` is a file on this machine by absolute path, copied there, or an upload in the project's `.tatolab/uploads/` by its SHA-256, moved there. The bytes replaced are kept as an upload under their SHA-256, so an undo puts them back with the earlier sidecar; history records the sidecar alone. A file replaced outside the runtime is not supported. Answers the asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`; bytes the sidecar already records apply nothing and are refused as an empty transaction. Refused for a stream asset, whose graph document graph edits change.

methods.name: create_stream
methods.summary: Create a stream in a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Create a stream in the project as one transaction: a new stream asset, its graph document written at `path` holding no nodes, its UUID, which the runtime makes, and its `display_name`. While the project runs, the new stream is loaded on the project's queue and the answer carries that load's `action`, which `describe_stream_action` follows. Answers the stream asset as `asset`, with the `transaction` and `commit`; an undo takes the document out and unloads the stream. Refused for a path another file holds or outside the project, and a blank `display_name`.

methods.name: delete_stream
methods.summary: Delete a stream from a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Delete a stream from the project as one transaction: its graph document leaves the project, recorded in the transaction so an undo writes it back and loads the stream again while the project runs, and its stream is unloaded and forgotten. Answers the stream asset as it was, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a UUID the project holds no stream asset under.

methods.name: set_stream_display_name
methods.summary: Set the name a stream is shown under, as one transaction.
methods.description: Show a stream under another display name as one transaction, written in its graph document so every machine the project is on shows it and an undo writes the earlier one. A loaded stream is shown under it at once and keeps its stream id. Answers the stream asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a blank `display_name`.

methods.name: add_dependency
methods.summary: Import another project into a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Import another project, as one transaction by `author`: the project `source` holds, a folder or a `.zip` of one on this machine, is copied whole into `imports/<folder>/` and recorded in `tatolab-project.json` under `dependencies` with the `version` its copy carries, the SHA-256 over its files. Nothing reaches the network. The copy is this project's own from then on: its assets are referenced as `{"asset": "<uuid>", "from": "<project uuid>"}` and read from its folder, its streams are placed with `use_dependency_stream`, and to edit it, open `imports/<folder>/` as a project of its own. Answers the `dependency`. Once it applies, a project with a `pyproject.toml` has its `.venv` made current on its stream action queue, a `make_venv_current` action that touches no stream, and its change feed carries `venv_made_current` once that is done, so the node types its imports install list. Refused, nothing copied, for a source holding no `tatolab-project.json` or no project UUID in it, naming what is missing, for this project itself, a project already imported, or a folder already held.

methods.name: update_dependency
methods.summary: Bring an imported project up to date with its source, as one transaction.
methods.description: Copy an import again, whole, as one transaction by `author`, from `source` or from the source it was last copied from, replacing its folder under `imports/` and its `version`. Every loaded stream holding one of its streams as a fragment follows the new copy. When files of its folder were edited since its copy, nothing changes: it answers them under `edited_files` with `overwrite_confirmation_needed`, and is sent again with `overwrite_edited_files` to overwrite them. Undo puts the folder back as it was. Once it applies, a project with a `pyproject.toml` has its `.venv` made current on its stream action queue, a `make_venv_current` action that touches no stream, and its change feed carries `venv_made_current` once that is done, so the node types its imports install list. Refused, nothing changed, for a project not imported, or a source holding another project.

methods.name: list_dependencies
methods.summary: List the projects a project imports.
methods.description: List the projects this one imports, each with its `folder`, `source` and `version` as `tatolab-project.json` holds them, and the files of its folder edited since its copy under `edited_files`; changes nothing. With `check_for_newer`, each source is read again and each import also answers `version_on_the_source` and `newer_version_exists`, or, for a source that could not be read, `check_refused_because`; nothing is copied until `update_dependency` copies it.

methods.name: remove_dependency
methods.summary: Take an imported project out of a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Stop importing a project, as one transaction by `author`: its folder leaves `imports/` and its entry `tatolab-project.json`; undo puts both back as they were. Answers the `dependency` as it was. Once it applies, a project with a `pyproject.toml` has its `.venv` made current on its stream action queue, a `make_venv_current` action that touches no stream, and its change feed carries `venv_made_current` once that is done, so its node types list without the import's. Refused, nothing changed, while a node of any of this project's streams — a fragment holding one of its streams, or a config holding `{"asset", "from"}` naming it, at any depth — still references it, naming each such node. Refused for a project not imported.

methods.name: use_dependency_stream
methods.summary: Place an imported project's stream in a loaded stream's graph as a fragment node, as one transaction.
methods.description: Place a stream of an imported project in a loaded stream's graph, as one committed transaction: a fragment node of type `tatolab.project:StreamFragment` whose config `{"stream": {"asset", "from"}}` references the stream. The graph document stores the reference alone; each load, and each change to the stream or its import, places the stream's nodes and links as its graph document under `imports/<folder>/` is on disk, each node under the UUID UUIDv5(fragment node's UUID, its own). Its Graph Input and Output nodes are the fragment's ports. Answers as `transact` does. Refused for a name a node of the graph already holds, and for a stream that holds the stream it is placed in, naming each stream of the cycle.

methods.name: list_project_files
methods.summary: List the files of a project that are not assets.
methods.description: List the project's files, or those under `under`, each by its path and length in bytes, sorted by path. Hidden folders such as `.tatolab/`, Python virtual environments, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/` and symbolic links are not listed.

methods.name: read_project_file
methods.summary: Read one file of a project.
methods.description: Read one of the project's files whole, answering its bytes as `content_base64`, standard base64 with padding, its `byte_len`, and its `content_sha256`, which a `write_project_file` sends back as `expected_sha256`. Refused for a path that is not a file of the project.

methods.name: create_node_file
methods.summary: Create a node file in a project from the template, as one transaction.
methods.description: Create a new node file of the project from the runtime's node template, as one transaction an undo reverses: a `@node.process` class in the current `tatolab.stream` idiom, named after the file, with one Image input `video_in` whose frames it hands on unchanged to one Image output `video_out`, each with its description. It loads as a node type of the project with no edits and `list_project_node_types` lists it at once. Answers the `path`, the `node_type` it declares — `<module>:<class>`, what `add_node` takes — and the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a path that already holds a file, that is not a `.py` file importable as a Python module, or whose class name the template cannot declare, and for every path `write_project_file` refuses.

methods.name: write_project_file
methods.summary: Write one file of a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Write one of the project's files whole, as one transaction: a new file is created with its folders, an existing one overwritten. An undo puts back what the file held, or takes a new file out. Answers the `path`, the `content_sha256` of the bytes written, and the `transaction` and `commit`. With `expected_sha256`, refused when the file changed or was taken out since it was read, so a save never overwrites another change. Content the file already holds is refused, as it changes nothing. Refused for what another tool changes — a stream's graph document, an asset's sidecar or bytes (`replace_asset`), `tatolab-project.json`, a file under `imports/` — and for a file inside a hidden folder or a Python virtual environment, which history does not record.

methods.name: list_project_node_types
methods.summary: List the node types a project offers, from its own node files and the packages it installs.
methods.description: List the node types and graph generators a project offers, read from source without running any of its code: its own node code outside `imports/`, each import's as its folder holds it now, and each installed distribution that declares `tatolab.nodes` entry points, each under `sources` by `source` (`project`, `dependency` or `installed_distribution`). A node type has its `type` (what `add_node` takes; an import's is led by its folder, `imports/<folder>/<module>:<class>`, and imported from there), `kind` (`process`, `function` or `shader`), `description`, `category` (the group its `@node.meta` files it under, a path where the group is inside another, as `Effects/Stylize`; null when it declares none, and for a Rust function node or an entry point whose declaration source does not show), and `inputs` and `outputs` where its declaration states them, each port's `family` null where source alone does not say. A graph generator has its `generator` (what `import_graph_generator` takes), its docstring as `description`, and its `promoted_config`. A module that does not parse is listed under its source's `unreadable_modules` with why and where; the rest still lists.

methods.name: list_project_views
methods.summary: List the Tato Studio views a project brings.
methods.description: List every Tato Studio view a project brings — each folder of its own `views/`, then of each import's `imports/<folder>/views/` — read from the folder's `tatolab_view.json` without running anything in it. Each view under `views` has its `view_type`, `<project name>:<view folder>`, which is a node type of each stream the project runs when the view opens and its `placement` is `node`; the `project`, `project_name` and `import_folder` (null for the project's own) of the project bringing it; its `view_folder_in_the_project`, the folder relative to the project, as `views/<folder>` or `imports/<import>/views/<folder>`, which names its files to a project file read; its `title`, `description`, `icon`, `preview` and `placement` (`area` or `node`); its declared `inputs` and `outputs`, each a `name`, a `family`, a `description` and an Array port's `range`; and its `manifest` as written. A folder whose manifest is missing, is not JSON, or does not read against view contract 1.0 is listed with `opens` false and why in `not_opened_because`; the rest still lists.

methods.name: write_studio_view_output
methods.summary: Write a value a Tato Studio view produced onto its node's output port. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`.
methods.description: Hand a value a Tato Studio panel wrote to the view node `node` of the stream `stream`, which publishes it on its output `port` to every link and viewer reading that port, stamped with stream time now. A view node is a node of a view type, `<project name>:<view folder>`, which each view of the stream's project or of one of its imports is when it opens and its `placement` is `node`; its ports are the view's declared inputs and outputs, and a panel reads its inputs with `open_viewer` on the port linked into each. Each Array, Channels or Records output of a view node has an input of its name, a setting read each run that takes no wire and holds no saved value, whose value the node publishes on the output; this call sets that input. Every write is published, stamped with stream time now, the same value written again as much as a new one, a Channels block starting where the last one written ended. A write is live data: the last value written is what a reader keeps, and a reader that connects later reads it, many panels may write one node and the last write wins, nothing is recorded in the graph document or the project's history, and the input returns to no value at Stop; a saved value on that input, by a `commit` set or an `add_node`'s `pins`, is refused, and one a graph document holds is dropped as the stream loads, with a warning naming the node and the input. `graph` renders the value as the input's live value. An Image or Packets output, which has no such input, is refused. Refused for a stream whose project is stopped, naming `start_playback`; a node of another type; a node that is not running; a node with no such output; `null`, which sets no value; and a value its port's family does not take, as `input_value_not_valid` at `/value`. A refusal because the node does not run comes with `structuredContent.refusal.not_running_because` naming why: `playback_stopped`, `playback_paused` (a node added while its project is paused), `preparing` or `node_failed`, the runtime's words beside it in `runtime_words`. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`, which this call is one `live` set of, naming the view node as `node` and the output as `input`.

methods.name: write_graph_input
methods.summary: Write a value onto one of a loaded stream's graph inputs. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`.
methods.description: Hand a value to the Input `input` of the stream `stream`: the stream's top-level `GraphInput` declaring it publishes the value on its `value` output to every node it is linked to, stamped with stream time now, and each reads it on its next process; every write is published, the same value written again as much as a new one, and a node linked later reads the last value set. A write is live data: many clients may write one Input and the last write wins, and nothing is recorded in the graph document or the project's history. An Input whose config's `lifetime` is `kept`, the default, keeps the last value in the project's store, so it carries it again after a Stop, a reload and a restart of the runtime; a `reset` Input returns to its saved value, its `default`, at Stop. While the project is stopped, a `kept` Input takes the value and carries it at the next Play, and `graph` shows it; a `reset` Input is refused as `playback_stopped`. Until a write, the Input carries its saved value, if it holds one. `graph` renders the value an Input carries now, or carries at the next Play while stopped, under its node's `graph_interface` component, as `current_value`. Array, Channels and Records Inputs are written; an Image or Packets Input runs nothing and is refused. Refused for an Input no top-level `GraphInput` declares, and a value its family does not take. A refusal because the Input's node does not run comes with `structuredContent.refusal.not_running_because` naming why: `playback_stopped`, `playback_paused` (a node added while its project is paused), `preparing` or `node_failed`, the runtime's words beside it in `runtime_words`. Replaced by `set_node_input_value`, which this call is one `live` set of, naming no node and the Input as `input`.

methods.name: import_project
methods.summary: Import a project from an archive into a folder that does not exist yet.
methods.description: Make a new project in `project_directory` from the `.zip` of a project at `source`, as a Marketplace entry or a GitHub archive is handed over. Its files are unpacked as `add_dependency` copies a zip — every file its history would record and every asset, its `imports/` included, never a hidden folder such as its `.tatolab/`, a cache, a Python virtual environment or a symbolic link — under a new project UUID of its own, so the same zip imported twice makes two projects, and committed by `author` as the first commit of a history of its own. Nothing reaches the network and nothing runs: open it with `open_project`, and `start_playback` plays it. Answers the new `project_directory`, its `project` UUID, its `name` and the `commit`. Refused, nothing left behind, for a relative path, a `source` that is a folder or no zip archive, a zip holding no `tatolab-project.json` or no project UUID in it, naming what is missing, or a `project_directory` that already exists.

methods.name: logs
methods.summary: Read a project's log records after a cursor, oldest first.
methods.description: Read a project's log records after the cursor `after`, oldest first, each as the project's JSONL log on disk holds it: every stream of the project and every load of it writes that one log, each record stamped with its `stream` — none for a load's own lines, uv's among them — across the runtime's runs, whether the stream is still recorded or not. `stream` narrows to one stream's records, and `action` to the records of one stream action — every record its load wrote, uv's among them, and the records of the streams it started. Pass the result's `next_after` back as `after` to read on; `records_no_longer_held` is true when retention deleted the segment `after` named, so the page resumes at the oldest record held. A project that has logged nothing answers no records.

methods.name: open_viewer
methods.summary: Open a viewer of a node's output port, held open for the connection that opened it.
methods.description: Open a viewer of any output port of a running node, adding no node and changing no graph: the runtime holds the port's channel open and answers the `viewer` id, the `iceoryx2_domain_root`, the `channel` whose reserved subscriber slot the viewer takes from its own process, and the `wake_service` the node notifies on each write, whose one listener the viewer takes so it waits for a message rather than reading on a timer. The answer's `viewer_reads` says which messages the viewer reads: `every_message` for a Channels port, in order as far back as the channel holds them for it, so a viewer can play the sound, and `latest_message` for every other family, skipping what it falls behind on; either way the channel overwrites what the viewer has not read, so it never slows the stream; an Image message names a pooled frame rather than carrying its pixels, and the viewer imports that frame's surface from the `surface_share_address` the way a helper process does. The viewer stays open until `close_viewer` or the end of the connection that opened it, so it is opened only over a connection that stays open: `/mcp/stdio` or `/control/ws`. Refused for a node that is not running, with `structuredContent.refusal.not_running_because` naming why: `playback_stopped`, `playback_paused` (a node added while its project is paused), `preparing` or `node_failed`, the runtime's words beside it in `runtime_words`.

methods.name: close_viewer
methods.summary: Close a viewer this connection opened.
methods.description: Close a viewer this connection opened, letting go of its port's channel.

methods.name: set_stream_clock_scale
methods.summary: Run a started stream's scaled clock at another scale from now on.
methods.description: Run a started stream's scaled clock at `scale` from now on: its stream time carries on from where it stands, never jumping or running backwards, and every node's `ctx.time`, write stamps and continuous pace follow the new scale. Above 1 the clock runs in steps of its `step_ns`, paced at the scale, behind the step barrier every node runs on; back at or under 1 it runs free again. Refused for a stream on the real or a stepped clock, and for a scale above 1 while the stream holds a node that paces itself (execution = manual) and is not paced by real time. Live only: the stream's next start runs the clock its graph document names.

methods.name: create_project
methods.summary: Queue the creation of a project from the starter or a sample.
methods.description: Create a project — the one `tatolab new` creates: the starter, its `tatolab-project.json`, one stream asset `streams/main.graph.json` holding the test pattern's one source, `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version` and `.gitignore`, or, given a `sample` that `list_samples` lists, a copy of that sample project under a new project UUID — committed as the first commit of the project's history, in `project_directory`, or with none in a folder `<adjective>-<noun>` drawn under `~/streams`, and queue its open, answering at once with the action's id as `action`, the stream id its `main` runs under as `stream`, and the resolved `project_directory`. The action writes the project's files, then opens it as `open_project` does — reads its graph documents, makes its `.venv`, however long uv takes, and holds its stream stopped until `start_playback` — the project named after its folder and its `main` stream shown under the folder's name. A directory already holding a file the create writes fails the action with nothing written. Follow it with `describe_stream_action` and `logs`; the project is recorded and re-loaded whenever the runtime starts, so a later session finds it in `list_streams`. Refused only for a `sample` the runtime unit does not carry, naming the ones it does, a relative `project_directory`, one that cannot be created, or, with none, a `HOME` that is unset or not absolute or a draw that finds no free folder.

methods.name: list_samples
methods.summary: List the sample projects a new project can be created from.
methods.description: List the sample projects the runtime unit carries at its own version, each by the `name` `create_project`'s `sample` takes, its `title` and a `summary` of what it shows, in name order: none for a runtime run outside a runtime unit.

methods.name: refresh_fragments
methods.summary: Refresh, as one transaction, every fragment whose graph generator a changed module defines.
methods.description: Refresh, as one transaction, every fragment of the project's loaded streams whose graph generator, or a generator nested in it, is defined in a module one of `changed_files` holds: each is run again with the promoted settings its fragment keeps, as `import_graph_generator` refreshes it, each node keeping its UUID by name. Answers as `transact` does; with no such fragment, it answers no operation and records no transaction. A generator that raises refuses the whole refresh with its traceback, nothing changed.

methods.name: undo
methods.summary: Undo an author's latest transaction in a project that is not undone yet, as a new transaction.
methods.description: Undo the latest transaction by `author` in the project that is not undone yet, applying its inverse as a new transaction: its graph edits to the running streams and their graph documents, its asset changes and file writes to the project. Only the author's own transactions are undone, so two authors' interleaved edits are each undone by their own author. An edit to a stream not loaded is applied to its graph document alone, and the stream of a stream document the undo takes out is unloaded and forgotten. Refused when the author has nothing left to undo, or when what it would undo no longer applies — a node another author removed since, or a stream document it would take out that was edited after it was written. Answers the transaction applied, with `undoes` naming the one it reversed.

methods.name: redo
methods.summary: Redo what an author's latest undo in a project reversed, as a new transaction.
methods.description: Redo what `author`'s latest undo in the project reversed, as a new transaction; a new edit by the author after the undo leaves nothing to redo. Answers the transaction applied, with `redoes` naming the one it reapplied.

x-agent-discovery-tools.name: list_operation_groups
x-agent-discovery-tools.summary: List every operation the runtime serves, by group.
x-agent-discovery-tools.description: List every operation this runtime serves, by group, each with its name and one sentence saying what it does. The tools in this tool list are the ones used most; every other operation — a project's assets, files, dependencies, node types and views, each single graph edit, redo, viewers — is reached through `call_operation`. Start here when no listed tool does what you need, then read the operation's params with `describe_operations`.

x-agent-discovery-tools.name: describe_operations
x-agent-discovery-tools.summary: Describe operations: what each does, the params it takes and what it answers.
x-agent-discovery-tools.description: Describe operations by name, or every operation of one group: what each reads, changes and answers, the JSON Schema of its params and of its result, whether it only reads, and the contract version it arrived in. Call it before the first `call_operation` of an operation, and send the params exactly as its `params_schema` states them.

x-agent-discovery-tools.name: call_operation
x-agent-discovery-tools.summary: Call any operation the runtime serves, by name.
x-agent-discovery-tools.description: Call any operation `list_operation_groups` lists, by name, with its `params`. It answers exactly what the operation answers, and a refusal is the operation's own. An operation that is also a listed tool answers the same either way.

studio.description: What Tato Studio draws the node with, under the studio contract: `position` an `[x, y]` pair of numbers, `group` a labelled group's UUID, `comment` and `colour` strings, `collapsed` a bool, and anything else a client keeps under `metadata`, an object kept as given. mode.description: `commit`, the default: the edit is applied to the running stream, written to the stream's graph document and recorded as one commit on the project's history, so it is kept on the next load and undo reverses it. `live`: applied to the running stream alone, never in history, and gone on the next load, except a value set live on a `kept` input, which is held across a Stop and the next load while a `reset` input forgets its one at Stop. Send a continuous gesture as one transaction when it ends.

author.description: Who the change is by, as history records it and undo follows it. Omit it to be the agent the MCP client named in its `clientInfo`.

idempotency_key.description: A key the caller mints once per user gesture, such as a slider drag committed on release. A `live` edit is never recorded, so its key is not kept.

stream.description: The stream the edit is to: the stream id `list_streams` answers as `stream`, or its stream asset's UUID, the `asset` its graph document holds, which `list_streams` reports as its `location`'s `stream_asset`. IntegerPinValue.description:
An Integer's stored value: a whole number, within its exact size when the type states one
and exact to 2^53 when it states none.

FloatPinValue.description: A Float's stored value: any JSON number; `1` is taken as 1.0.

StringPinValue.description: A String's stored value: any text; the empty string is a value.

MenuPinValue.description: A Menu's stored value: one of the type's option names, spelled as declared.

ColorPinValue.description:
A Color's stored value: sRGB red, green and blue and alpha, each 0 for none and 1 for full,
not linear light and not multiplied by alpha. Alpha 1 is opaque. A number outside 0 to 1 is
taken as sent.

z.description: Present for three and four components.

VectorPinValue.description:
A Vector's stored value: `x` and `y`, with `z` for three components and `w` for four, and no
other key. The type's declared size says which keys it holds.

RectanglePinValue.description:
A Rectangle's stored value: its left edge `x`, its top edge `y`, and a `width` and `height`
of 0 or more. The node says whether they are pixels or a share of the frame.

TransformPinValue.description:
A Transform's stored value: a 4 by 4 matrix as 16 numbers, row by row. It multiplies a
column, so the fourth number of each of the first three rows is the translation.

from.description: The UUID of the imported project that holds the asset; absent, the project's own.

AssetPinValue.description:
An Asset's stored value: the asset's UUID as `list_assets` answers it, with `from`, the
import's project UUID, for an asset of an import. Never a bare string.

ListPinValue.description: A List's stored value: a list of its element's form, in order. `[]` is a value.

BundlePinValue.description:
A bundle's stored value: an object keyed by member name, each member in its own type's form.
Only a member that declares a default may be left out.
